evidence_cards.document_title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
evidence_cards.main_contribution: TGN (Temporal Graph Networks) proposes a generic framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events, combining memory modules and graph-based operators for efficient temporal graph representation learning.
overlaps: Addresses representation learning on dynamic/temporal graphs, overlapping with the novelty point's goal of learning representations of sequential graphs
Models dynamic graphs as sequences of timed events, conceptually similar to modeling sequential graphs as snapshots over time
Aims for computational efficiency, similar to the novelty point's goal of reducing memory and training time

sources.quote: we present Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs), a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events. Thanks to a novel combination of memory modules and graph-based operators, TGNs are able to significantly outperform previous approaches being at the same time more computationally efficient.

evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
evidence_cards.main_contribution: AGL proposes a scalable system for industrial-purpose graph machine learning that generates k-hop neighborhood subgraphs for each node and performs distributed GNN training on parameter servers, partitioning the large graph into information-complete subgraphs assigned to worker nodes.
overlaps: Partitions a large graph into subgraphs for distributed processing
Assigns partitioned subgraphs to worker nodes for GNN training
Supports large-scale graph data processing for GNN training

sources.quote: We design to generate the $k$-hop neighborhood, an information-complete subgraph for each node, as well as do the inference simply by merging values from in-edge neighbors and propagating values to out-edge neighbors via MapReduce.
